title: Reaper ↔ DuckOS system service contracts
purpose: Versioned host-call contracts for a downstream DuckOS integration. This registry defines boundaries and acceptance criteria; it does not provide executable handlers.

compatibility.most_function_registry: Separate registry. Existing MOST-FN-111 through MOST-FN-130 retain their current meanings and identifiers.
compatibility.reaper_runtime: No new callable runtime functions are introduced by this manifest.
compatibility.implementation_owner: DuckOS owns kernel, driver, service and package implementations. Reaper owns language, effect, type and host-call ABI contracts.

status_model.planned: Contract and acceptance criteria exist; no implementation claim is made.
status_model.experimental: An implementation exists for a declared target subset and is clearly target-gated.
status_model.delivered: Implementation, negative tests, target evidence and required CI all pass.

safety_invariants: Spawn only from an approved service definition
Do not expose fork or descriptor mutation to ordinary Reaper code
Record service identity and inherited handles
Validate hook ownership and lifetime
Define start, stop, reload ordering and re-entrancy
Never invoke callbacks while holding the registry lock
Keep civil-time schedules distinct from monotonic deadlines
Define timezone and daylight-saving behavior
Bound job count, execution time and retry policy
Use bounded records and an explicit overflow policy
Keep producer paths non-blocking where required
Attach timestamp source, process identity and severity as typed fields
acceptance: Ring overflow and loss accounting tests
Malformed and oversized record rejection tests

safety_invariants: Resolve and validate the full dependency DAG before side effects
Reject dependency cycles and unavailable requirements
Make start idempotent and report partial activation
Use an explicit shutdown state machine and caller deadline
Flush filesystems and devices through their owners
Do not use a fixed delay or unconditional global process kill
Keep recovery entry distinct from disabling interrupts
Preserve console and diagnostic paths
Require kernel-owned safe-state transitions before launching recovery tools
acceptance: Recovery from service and driver failure tests

safety_invariants: Treat add/remove notifications as untrusted and repeatable
Match only approved device identities and driver manifests
Never install or load arbitrary driver code as a side effect of an event

services.owner: DuckOS firmware broker plus device driver
safety_invariants: Verify signature, digest, hardware identity and revision before staging
Use a device-specific update protocol and explicit authorization
Preserve recovery or rollback behavior for interrupted updates
acceptance: Invalid signature and target mismatch tests

safety_invariants: Validate RSDP and table checksums, lengths, alignment and mapped ranges
Keep AML parsing/interpreting separate from table discovery
Never trust firmware-provided pointers or AML

services.owner: DuckOS NPU driver and user-mode runtime
safety_invariants: Discover devices through the device manager rather than a fixed path
Negotiate firmware, queue, DMA and memory budgets
Tie sessions and DMA buffers to explicit owners and lifetimes
Validate rank, dimensions, layout, dtype and overflow before dispatch
Use explicit session and buffer handles
Require fence completion, timeout and device-loss handling
acceptance: CPU/NPU parity tests for supported dtypes

safety_invariants: Validate graph topology and supported operators before execution
Bound scratch memory, tensor sizes, execution steps and time
Fail on unsupported operators rather than silently skipping layers
Treat model files and external tensor data as untrusted input
Limit file size, protobuf depth, tensor dimensions and external-data paths
Declare supported ONNX opsets and operator coverage
Name the supported encryption scheme, parameters and threat model
Keep ciphertext, plaintext and key handles as distinct types
Reject unsupported operations; never imply generic homomorphic inference

services.owner: DuckOS container service plus kernel isolation adapters
safety_invariants: Define isolation primitives in DuckOS rather than assuming Linux clone/chroot
Verify image digest and mount policy before execution
Apply CPU, memory, process, filesystem and network budgets
acceptance: Image integrity and mount traversal tests

services.owner: DuckOS hypervisor service and architecture backend
safety_invariants: Use a versioned hypervisor ABI; KVM is only a Linux backend
Validate memory regions, alignment, CPU features and device model
Bound vCPU, RAM and device resources and define teardown semantics
Keep Flatpak import optional and separate from the native package format
Verify bundle identity, signatures and declared permissions
Never execute install hooks during inspection or verification
Use signed repositories and explicit trust roots
Resolve dependencies before mutation and install transactionally
Support offline cache, rollback and deterministic package identity
Select an immutable target profile and pinned toolchain
Pass executable and arguments as an argv vector, never a concatenated shell string
Record source revision, toolchain digest, target ABI and reproducible output hashes
